changes: Preserved the accepted SAS construction, monthly OLS/Fama–MacBeth xtfmb estimator, predictor definitions, windows, tie handling, and Stata output architecture. Rebuilt the original 1966-07 through 2002-12 panel jointly with the requested 2003-01 through 2007-12 addition using the current local versions of the same eight named sources.

Kept the original 1966-07 fit start and raw-return history from 1963-07; extended raw/input upper bounds and fit end through 2007-12-31. The selected daily FX lookback, annual availability lag, 12-month refresh, and all return/trading-month logic are unchanged.
Added post-estimation counts from each fit’s e(sample), split at 2003-01, and generated one aggregate-only CSV per panel during the native Stata cell.
limitations: The sample record describes an intersection of the 2002 Compustat and CRSP tapes, while this authorized replay uses current local vintages. No frozen 2002 source snapshot or explicit fixed identifier cohort is staged; historical revisions and post-2002 cohort composition may therefore differ from the article’s original tape-based sample.

The paper’s broad sample statement begins July 1964, but the assigned Table 5 Model 4 fits begin July 1966 and the accepted construction reads returns from July 1963 to form the t−36:t−13 return control for the first fit month. The Table 5 note’s t−13 endpoint is retained over the conflicting body-text t−12 description, as documented in the accepted design.

The paper names Fama–MacBeth but does not specify the estimator within each month; the accepted reconstruction uses unweighted OLS. The assigned predecessor outcome confirms the three fits executed but does not contain their native focal coefficients, so each comparison will use the paper-reported Table 5 coefficient from the assigned model-results record and the fresh extended estimate.
